question: Does the design hold — extension-owned real-message bootstrap via sendUserMessage, taskless greet restored, single-owner gate preserved — ready to baseline implementation?

artifacts.summary: Ideation complete (worker 79eb0de5, commit 0951ab783, pushed). Mechanism (a) selected and spike-verified FIRST: the spacedock pi extension sends FO_BOOTSTRAP_TEXT as a real first-turn user message via pi.sendUserMessage() at session_start, gated on a new env-only frontdoor marker PI_SPACEDOCK_LAUNCH_TASKLESS=1 (set only when no operator task is given) — frontdoor stays argv-and-env-only, AC-3 intact, greet text remains extension-owned; expandPromptTemplates rejected with rationale. Live TUI spike on installed pi 0.85.1: positive arm delivered a persisted first-turn user message and booted the model turn with zero operator input; control arm (no markers) stayed silent (empty session, 0 turns) — single-owner gate preserved. Existing context-hook bootstrap retained as fallback when the send throws (throwing-fake unit case, AC-5); compaction boot-record arm untouched; the once-per-turn request-time-only ephemerality is fixed on the primary path (real message persists). ACs lean per the no-test-infra directive: AC-1 value (taskless launch greets within 60s vs today's 0-turn silent baseline, across wrap/dev-override shapes), AC-2 gate (plain pi receives nothing), proofs = four one-off live launch arms + extensions of the two existing test owners (test/spacedock.test.ts, internal/cli/pi_frontdoor_test.go), no new harness.
